rule_name: Ration a Character's Verbal Tic to the Moments It Characterises
quote: She spends nineteen days on it
why: exact-duration counting applied by the narration to a scene with no anxiety, control, or dissociation payoff, using the tic as reflexive default rather than as signal
suggestion: She works through the logs, two tables of them, until the pattern gives.

rule_name: Ration a Character's Verbal Tic to the Moments It Characterises
quote: talks her through it for twenty minutes
why: another instance of the narration naming an exact duration as background texture, unattached to any character-specific meaning, the drift the rule warns against
suggestion: talks her through it, unhurried, until she has it

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
why: a universal vague duration marker from the same banned family as "for a second" / "for a while", used regardless of what kind of moment is being timed
suggestion: Make it noisy for a shift change and that's a camera being a camera.

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
quote: You went left again, and you went left last time as well.
why: opens a four-turn exchange (lines 97, 99, 101, 103) carrying only one attribution/action beat, at the very end, the same unbroken four-line-one-tag pattern the rule names as the failure case
suggestion: give the middle an anchor, e.g. "Chloe pushes a counter forward. 'I went left because you'd worked out I go left, so left was the surprise.'"

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
why: opens a four-turn exchange (lines 13, 15, 17, 19) with only one tag arriving at the last line, matching the rule's own banned four-turn/one-tag example
suggestion: add a small beat partway through, e.g. '"Why, though?" Marek does not look up from the desk.'
